chapter.title: Props in Practice
chapter.description: Spreading props, forwarding the rest, and building a reusable component.

blocks.text: Two patterns show up constantly once you start building shared components.
The spread operator forwards an entire object as props. It is handy when a parent already holds the right shape, and dangerous when you lose track of what is being passed.
A wrapper component usually pulls out the props it cares about and forwards everything else to the underlying element. That keeps the wrapper usable anywhere the plain element would be.
Put `{...rest}` before your own props if callers should not be able to override them, and after if they should. Order decides who wins.

blocks.title: Build a reusable price formatter
blocks.instructions: Complete formatPrice so it returns a string like $12.50. Use toFixed(2) and prefix with a dollar sign.

items: Components should do one job and be declared at module level.
Props flow down from parent to child and are read only.
`children` turns a component into a container other components can fill.
Rest props let a wrapper stay as flexible as the element it wraps.

blocks.text: Anything you put between a component's opening and closing tags arrives as a prop named `children`. This is what makes React components composable.
When a component grows a long list of boolean props, that is usually a sign it should accept content instead of options.

blocks.code:
// Configuration: every new variation needs another prop
<Dialog
  hasHeader
  hasFooter
  showCloseButton
  footerButtonLabel="Save"
/>

// Composition: the caller supplies whatever it needs
<Dialog>
  <Dialog.Header>Edit profile</Dialog.Header>
  <Dialog.Body><ProfileForm /></Dialog.Body>
  <Dialog.Footer><button>Save</button></Dialog.Footer>
</Dialog>

blocks.text: `children` is just a prop, so nothing stops you from passing several pieces of UI under different names.
Passing elements as props is also the simplest fix for prop drilling: instead of threading data through three layers, hand the finished element down from where the data already lives.
